domain: Subtracting fractions, mixed numbers, and whole numbers with simplification

skills.name: Prepare operands for subtraction
skills.definition: Rewrite operands into a subtraction-ready form before computing, including finding common denominators and normalizing whole numbers or nonstandard mixed numbers.
skills.merge_rationale: S01 and S02 are both setup/preparation skills applied before subtraction. In the dossiers, both serve the same instructional phase: making operands compatible for later subtraction. They are distinct at fine grain, but at K=5 the diagnostic distinction between denominator alignment and operand-format normalization can be coarsened without collapsing setup with execution.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Carry out subtraction once operands are in compatible form, including subtracting numerators over a common denominator and subtracting whole and fractional parts of mixed numbers.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because it is the core execution skill and has distinct error patterns from setup, regrouping, and post-processing.

skills.name: Regroup whole to fraction
skills.definition: Borrow one whole and convert it into fractional units when the fractional part of the minuend is insufficient for direct subtraction.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because regrouping is a major diagnostic breakpoint with characteristic borrowing errors that differ from direct subtraction.

skills.name: Simplify result
skills.definition: Reduce the computed result to lowest terms or remove zero-valued fractional parts to express a standard numerical result.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because simplification has its own error profile and does not always occur.

skills.name: Compose final answer
skills.definition: Assemble computed whole and fractional parts and state the final answer in standard form.
skills.merge_rationale: Kept separate because final composition/presentation is a post-processing step distinct from arithmetic and simplification.
